text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
Naturalist GEORGE CALEY, who explored the Sydney area after coming to Australia and made two attempts to cross the Blue Mountains, was born in 1770.
Leading Australian temperance evangelist and world missionary BESSIE LEE was born in 1860.
German-born American composer FREDERICK LOEWE, who, in collaboration with ALAN JAY LERNER wrote the music for "Brigadoon", "My Fair Lady" and "Gigi", was born in 1901.
West Australian mining magnate LANG (LANGLEY GEORGE) HANCOCK, who was responsible for the discovery and development of the state's iron ore industry, was born in 1909.
Greek-born PRINCE PHILLIP MOUNTBATTEN, the DUKE OF EDINBURGH (and husband of QUEEN ELIZABETH II), was born in 1921.

American actress/singer JUDY GARLAND (born FRANCES GUMM) was born in 1922. She played her first part in "Broadway Melody Of 1938" (1937), and her singing of "Somewhere Over The Rainbow" in the classic "Wizard Of Oz" (1939) made her world famous. She died in London on the 22nd of June, 1969.
Former Federal National Party leader (and reported jazz fan) IAN MCCAHON SINCLAIR was born in 1929.
** EVENTS **
1692 : The first witch trials were concluded in the

Massachusetts town of Salem. Two alleged witches were hanged, but the witch-hunt was so intense that many women in the area felt unsafe, fearing they too would be accused. The witch trials were presided over by judges SAMUEL SEWELL, JOHN HATHORNE and WILLIAM STOUGHTON.
1727 : KING GEORGE I of England, who took the throne in
1714 following the death of QUEEN ANNE, died.
1829 : The rivalry between England's two most prestigious universities, Oxford and Cambridge took to the water, with the first rowing regatta at Henley on the Thames River.
1924 : Italian socialist leader GIACOMO MATTEOTTI was assassinated by MUSSOLINI's facists.
1933 : The "Australian Women's Weekly", published by FRANK PACKER, went on sale for the first time.
1954 : An aerial search party found more than 100,000 people isolated from the world in the Papua New Guinea highlands. The community was surrounded by sheer limestone cliffs.
1960 : 29 people were killed when a Fokker Friendship aircraft crashed at Mackay on the central Queensland coast.
1965 : A British 'European Airways' de Havilland jet flying from Paris to London, made the first landing by automatic control.
1967 : The '6-day' war between Israel and its Arab neighbours ended, with the Israelis securing a 200 per cent expansion in the territory they held.
1967 : American actor SPENCER TRACY died. He once said: "There were times when my pants were so thin I could sit on a dime and tell you if it was heads or tails".
1972 : The SAMMY DAVIS Junior song "Candy Man" became an instant international hit, leading the American charts for two weeks.
1985 : CLAUS VON BULOW was found not guilty of attempting to murder his wife SUNNY by giving her an overdose of insulin. At the time, it was claimed he was trying to inherit her vast fortune.
1986 : Irish pop singer BOB GELDOF and American philanthropist JOHN PAUL GETTY II were given honorary knighthoods by QUEEN ELIZABETH II.
1987 : Britain expelled two Iranian envoys, (four more were expelled a week later) after the mistreatment of British envoy EDWARD CHAPLIN.
